parts.final_form: straight line, positive gradient, in quadrants 1, 3 and 4 (perpendicular bisector of 2i and 3)
parts.ms: M1 a non-horizontal, non-vertical line not through O; A1 correct position (MS p.17)
parts.er: Most recognised a perpendicular bisector but sketches lacked clarity; indicate which line is the locus (ER p.5)

parts.ask: T: w = iz/(z − 2i), z ≠ 2i, maps the locus to a circle C: find C as |w − (p + qi)| = r
parts.ms: M1 z = 2wi/(w − i); dM1 w = u + iv with conjugate (or substitute into the locus); A1 z in real and imaginary parts (or −2 = 2wi − 3w + 3i); ddM1 into y = (3/2)x − 5/4 (or Pythagoras on the moduli); dddM1 completes the square on 13u² + 13v² + 12u − 18v + 5 = 0; A1. Way 3 isolates w directly: |2i − 3||w + 3i/(2i − 3)| = 2 (MS pp.17–20)
parts.er: Demanding: z in terms of w nearly always found, but the algebra defeated many and the required form was rare; some substituted only numerators; Way 3 users dropped the modulus signs (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Use de Moivre to show cos 5x ≡ cos x(a sin⁴x + b sin²x + c), integers a, b, c
parts.ms: M1 real terms of (cos x + i sin x)⁵ with binomial coefficients; A1 cos⁵x − 10cos³x sin²x + 5cos x sin⁴x; M1 cos²x = 1 − sin²x; A1 (MS p.21)
parts.er: Mostly fine; a few omitted binomial coefficients, used multiple-angle formulae, or the (z + 1/z)ⁿ route; sign and coefficient slips (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Hence solve cos 5θ = sin 2θ sin θ − cos θ for 0 < θ < π/2, to 3 d.p. (all working shown)
parts.ms: M1 uses (a) and sin 2θ = 2sin θ cos θ to reach cos θ(16sin⁴θ − 14sin²θ + 2) = 0; dM1 sin²θ = (7 ± √17)/16, square roots; ddM1 θ values; A1 awrt 0.986, 0.438 (MS pp.21–22)
parts.er: Often unanswered; square root forgotten (values of sin²θ used as sin θ); values appeared without working, presumably from a calculator; show all working (ER pp.3, 6)

parts.ask: r = 1 − sin θ, 0 ≤ θ < π/2; the tangent at P is parallel to the initial line: find the polar coordinates of P
parts.ms: M1 differentiates r sin θ = sin θ − sin²θ (r cos θ is M0); A1 cos θ − 2sin θ cos θ; dM1 solves, sin θ = 1/2; A1 both coordinates, r seen in (a) (MS p.23)
parts.er: Most used y = r sin θ correctly; a few stopped at θ without r (ER p.6)

parts.ask: R is bounded by θ = π/2, the tangent at P, the curve and the initial line: show the area of R is (1/32)(aπ + b√3 + c), integers a, b, c
parts.ms: M1 ½∫(1 − sin θ)²dθ with sin²θ = ½ − ½cos 2θ; A1 3θ/2 + 2cos θ − ¼sin 2θ; M1 limits 0 and π/6; M1 triangle ½(½cos π/6)(½sin π/6) = √3/32; dM1 sector plus triangle; A1 cao. Way 2: limits 0 to π/2 and subtract the area above the curve (MS pp.23–24)
parts.er: Integration usually right (main loss: sign in the cos 2θ formula); limits π/6 and 0 most successful, 0 to π/2 caused difficulties; triangle sometimes without working; slips combining the π and √3 terms (ER p.6)

parts.ask: x = t^(1/2): find dy/dx in terms of y and t
parts.ms: M1 chain rule; A1. Printed (5) covers (a)(i) and (a)(ii); the scheme marks (i) M1A1 and (ii) dM1A1A1 (MS p.25)
parts.er: Quite well done; some left it in x; reciprocal of ½t^(−1/2) mishandled (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find d²y/dx² in terms of y and t
parts.ms: dM1 product rule on k t^(1/2) dy/dt with dt/dx; A1 any correct expression; A1 in y and t only. Working in x and t: SC (MS pp.25–26)
parts.er: Less successful: differentiated w.r.t. t instead of x; a factor dt/dx often omitted; x-and-t versions rarely converted back (ER pp.6–7)

parts.ask: Hence show x = t^(1/2) (t > 0) transforms x y″ − (6x² + 1)y′ + 9x³y = x⁵ (I) into 4y″(t) − 12y′(t) + 9y = t (II)
parts.final_form: given result with an intermediate line
parts.ms: M1 substitutes (a) and replaces x by t^(1/2); A1* at least one intermediate line (MS pp.25–26)
parts.er: Some jumped from substitution to the answer and lost the A; show intermediate steps in "show that" (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Solve (II) for a general solution y in terms of t
parts.ms: M1 4m² − 12m + 9 = 0, m = 3/2; A1 CF e^(3t/2)(At + B); M1 PI at + b (PI = at is M0); dM1 compares coefficients; A1 GS in t with "y =". (c) and (d) marked together (MS p.26)
parts.er: Most successful part; wrong CF form; common error PI = at (lost three marks); mixed t and x; missing "y =" or GS left in x (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Hence find the general solution of (I)
parts.ms: B1ft replaces t by x² in their (c), with "y =" (MS p.26)
parts.er: Mostly earned (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Show 2/(√r + √(r − 2)) = √r − √(r − 2) for r ≥ 2 (no calculator)
parts.ms: M1 multiplies by (√r − √(r−2))/(√r − √(r−2)) (either direction); A1* a non-given intermediate result seen; equivalence chains need a minimal conclusion (MS p.7)
parts.er: Most challenging part of Q1: some tried partial fractions or tested values of r; cross-multiplying with equivalences rarely scored both marks because the conclusion was missing (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Hence use the method of differences to find Σ_{r=2}^{n} 2/(√r + √(r − 2)) in simplest form
parts.ms: M1 any three of the rows r = 2, 3, 4, n−2, n−1, n with a cancelling pair; A1 correct algebraic or constant terms (−1 − 0 unsimplified OK); A1 simplified (√1 to 1) (MS p.7)
parts.er: Generally very well answered; errors came from not writing rows r = n − 1 and r = n, sign slips (√n − √(n−1) − 1 common), or a stray −2 (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Hence show Σ_{r=4}^{50} 2/(√r + √(r − 2)) = A + B√2 + C√3, integers A, B, C
parts.ms: M1 f(50) − f(3) using (b) (f(50) − f(4) is M0); A1. Decimal 10.9248… without the method: 0/2 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Some used (a) instead of (b), or the summand at 50 and 3; a few restarted the differences with n = 50; algebra slips in simplifying (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: z1 = (cos 5π/12 + i sin 5π/12)⁴ / (cos π/3 − i sin π/3)³: without a calculator show z1 = cos 2π/3 + i sin 2π/3
parts.final_form: given result via e.g. cos 8π/3 + i sin 8π/3
parts.ms: M1 one correct use of de Moivre; A1 both in polar form (numerator 20π/12; denominator cos(−π) + i sin(−π), the minus sign dealt with); M1 division by subtracting arguments (adding is M0); A1cso via 8π/3, no errors (MS pp.8–9)
parts.er: Hardest question on the paper (ER p.10); the only one with a mean below half marks (about 4.5/10) and a mode below full marks (ER p.4). The denominator minus sign was often not handled; going straight to cos π + i sin π reached the answer through wrong work (no credit); arguments added when dividing; exponential form most efficient but rarely used; show every step in "show that" (ER pp.4–5)

parts.ask: Shade on one Argand diagram the region R: |z − z1| ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ arg(z − z1) ≤ 3π/4
parts.final_form: sector of the unit circle centred at z1 (in Q2, through O) between the horizontal half-line and the half-line of gradient −1
parts.ms: M1 a circle; M1 two half-lines from the centre, one horizontal (not the real axis) and one of negative gradient; M1 shades inside the circle between them, anticlockwise from the horizontal; A1 correct sector in quadrants 1 and 2, circle centre in Q2 passing roughly through O (MS pp.8–9)
parts.er: Circle almost always seen; half-lines less successful: real axis used as a line or lines not meeting at the centre; final mark often lost because the circle must pass through the origin; ambiguous or missing shading (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Given z lies in R, find the smallest possible positive value of arg z
parts.ms: M1 identifies the 3 o'clock point (1/2, √3/2) of the sector and attempts the angle, e.g. arctan((√3/2)/(1/2)); A1 (MS pp.8–9)
parts.er: Good discriminator; often not attempted; successful answers built a triangle and used tan; some attempts did not match their diagram (ER p.5)

parts.ask: (x + 2)/(x + 4) ≤ x/(k(x − 1)), k > 0: show (x + 4)(x − 1)(px² + qx + r) ≤ 0 with p, q, r in terms of k (no calculator)
parts.final_form: p = k − 1, q = k − 4, r = −2k (positive multiples accepted)
parts.ms: M1 multiplies by k(x + 4)²(x − 1)² (or common denominator) and collects; dM1 factorises (x + 4)(x − 1) and expands to a 3TQ in x with k; A1cso no incorrect statement, correct inequality sign (MS p.10)
parts.er: Most cross-multiplied by squared factors, often with k² (unnecessary as k > 0); a common denominator was rarer; many algebraic slips with k (ER pp.5–6)

parts.ask: Hence or otherwise find the values of x with (x + 2)/(x + 4) ≤ x/(3(x − 1))
parts.ms: M1 k = 3: 2x² − x − 6 = 0, x = −3/2, 2; dM1 chooses the two regions between the two smaller and the two larger CVs; A1 both regions (signs condoned); A1 fully correct; ∩ in set notation loses the last mark (MS p.10)
parts.er: Many restarted (b) successfully; "outsides and middle" regions chosen; most common loss: including −4 and 1 in the regions (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the general solution of y″ − 8y′ + 16y = 48x² − 34
parts.ms: M1 (m − 4)² = 0; A1 CF (A + Bx)e^(4x); B1 PI λx² + μx + ν; M1 differentiates, substitutes, compares coefficients; A1ft GS ("GS =" instead of "y =" loses this) (MS p.11)
parts.er: Repeated root handled well, though a few wrote (A + B)e^(4x); some PIs had only two terms; arithmetic slips in the PI constant cost three A marks; some wrote "GS =" (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Given y = 4 and dy/dx = 21 at x = 0, find the particular solution
parts.ms: M1 uses (0, 4) (A = 5); M1 differentiates GS with product rule on Bxe^(4x); M1 uses y′(0) = 21 to find B = −2; A1 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Well answered; expanded CF form Ae^(4x) + Bxe^(4x) gave fewer differentiation slips; a few found y″(0) as if for a Taylor series (ER pp.6–7)

parts.ask: Hence find y at x = −2 in the form pe^q + r, integers p, q, r
parts.ms: M1 substitutes x = −2 into their PS, terms gathered; A1 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Little problem for those reaching it; occasional partial substitution (ER p.7)

parts.ask: T: w = (z + 1)/(z − 3), z ≠ 3, maps y = 4x onto a circle C: show C is 3u² + 3v² − 2u + v + k = 0 and find k
parts.ms: M1A1 z = (3w + 1)/(w − 1); dM1 w = u + iv and rationalises; ddM1 real and imaginary parts give x and y, then y = 4x; A1cso* k = −1, no incorrect statements (wrong z = (3w+1)/(1−w) loses both A marks). Alts: substitute z = x + 4xi (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Hence find (i) the centre and (ii) the radius of C
parts.ms: B1 centre or radius; B1 both, fractions simplified (allowed even if k = −1 was guessed) (MS p.12)
parts.er: Centre usually right (occasional sign slips); slips working out the radius (ER p.7)

parts.ask: y = sec x: show d³y/dx³ = sec x tan x(p sec²x + q), integers p, q
parts.ms: M1 second derivative (sec x tan²x + sec³x, or 2sec³x − sec x); dM1 third derivative; ddM1 correct form with valid identities; A1 (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Routine for most; many lost a power of tan or sec at the third derivative (chain rule) and scored 1/4; sin/cos approaches usually went wrong (ER p.8)

parts.ask: Hence find the Taylor series about π/3 of sec x up to (x − π/3)³, coefficients simplified
parts.ms: M1 values 2, 2√3, 14, 46√3 at π/3; dM1 correct Taylor formula with all four values; A1 simplified, needs a correct third derivative in (a) ("y =" not required) (MS pp.14–15)
